claims.text: A reversible decision can be undone later at a small cost and deserves a quick choice; a decision costly to undo deserves more evidence, or a shape that keeps it reversible.

ADR 0012 (one deployment for every shop) was decided before the number of shops or a large shop's contract demands were known; 1,000 shops are planned and a separate copy for a shop is a review condition.

claims.text: ADR 0024 was proposed at the start of Sprint 23 and decided at the end of its first week; production cannot yet email customers (Mailpit in the lab only catches email).
A reduced ATAM session (whole team and product owner) evaluated the shape ADR 0012 chose, at the end of Sprint 18 (assumed), just after 0012 was accepted and before building on it.
Waiting for certainty usually lets a decision happen by default, e.g. the first shop arriving on whatever shape the system has then.
ADR 0013 (shop data in shared tables) and ADR 0019 (release strategy) build on ADR 0012.

claims.text: ADR 0024 consequences: Notifications keeps IEmailSender and MailKitEmailSender; for sending, connecting to A adds TLS and login settings in SmtpSettings, no library change; then changing email service is a change of SMTP settings.
A calls back into the system for each bounced email and Notifications uses it to stop sending to that address; this is done when A is connected.
Lesson's reading, not stated in ADR 0024: a new email service's bounce report would have to be wired to Notifications again, so not everything stays in SMTP settings; §6 row 3 risk says the same.

SMTP is the standard protocol a program uses to hand an email to a mail server. At stage-4 IEmailSender is the interface Notifications sends through; MailKitEmailSender implements it with MailKit's SmtpClient; SmtpSettings holds the SMTP server's host and port.
claims.source_hint: RFC 5321 §1-2; DonHang.Notifications/IEmailSender.cs and MailKitEmailSender.cs @ stage-4 lines 7-28

claims.text: ADR 0024 is reviewed when inbox delivery falls below the assumed rate, A's price exceeds the assumed TCO, or A stops accepting email over SMTP.
ADR 0021's three reopen conditions: a contract requiring encryption of calls inside the cluster; services from several teams or languages; services calling each other across clusters.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0021-chua-dung-service-mesh.md @ stage-4 'Ba điều kiện mở lại'; docs/team/architecture-governance.md @ stage-4 lines 68-70

claims.text: The watched-assumptions table ("Giả định cần theo dõi") lists, for the ADRs it covers, assumption, reopen signal, where it shows and watching role; signals are copied from the ADR's review conditions; a signal leads to a new ADR, the old one is not rewritten.

ADR 0012's first signal (a shop contract demanding its own copy) shows in the shop's contract before signing, watched by the product owner; ADR 0022's price signal is watched by the team lead on the provider's invoice, ADR 0024's price signal on A's invoice.
Each quarter, with technical-strategy.md and roadmap.md, the team adds new ADRs with reopen conditions to the table, checks which signals have appeared, and checks the decision-rights table.
In the email evaluation, any option that cannot take email over SMTP with TLS and login is dropped (knock-out criterion L1); all three options pass it.

Trade-offs: choosing quickly fits cheap-to-undo choices; more evidence fits decisions others build on; a reversible shape fits when the options share a common interface; waiting fits only when nothing is built on one option meanwhile.
ADR 0012 expects that a shop whose contract demands its own copy gets a separate copy of the same system while other shops are served as before.

claims.text: ADR 0021: a mesh adds a proxy in every Pod and a controller to upgrade, and a bad mesh change can break calls between every service at once; option C encrypts only the Gateway-to-api hop and is done first if only encryption is required.

claims.text: Depth of analysis should follow the cost of undoing; a decision is judged by what was known and written when taken, not by an assumption later proving wrong.
ADR 0021's first assumption: no requirement asks for encryption inside the cluster; its signal shows in shop contracts, watched by the product owner.
